title: Your first math module
brief: Build calc.h, calc.c and main.c. Declare square(int) in the header, define it once in calc.c and call it from main.
hints: Put a prototype inside an include guard.
Define square in calc.c, including the header.
Compile main.c and calc.c together.

title: Squares and cubes across files
brief: Keep square(int) and add cube(int) as a second function exported by calc.h and implemented in calc.c.
hints: Expose both function prototypes in the guarded header.
Implement cube in the source file, not in the header.
Call the two exported functions from main.

title: A reproducible number stream
brief: Simulate N steps of a deterministic generator: state = (state*17+11)%97. Print the final state. Do not use rand().
input: Two integers: seed in [0,96], N in [0,30].
hints: Initialize state with the supplied seed.
Update state exactly N times.
Modulo 97 keeps state inside [0,96].

title: Count even and odd generator states
brief: Keep the generator, and count even and odd states produced AFTER each update. The original seed is never counted.
input: Two integers: seed in [0,96], N in [0,30].
hints: Preserve the original state update.
Inspect state modulo two after each update.
even + odd must equal N.

title: Save then inspect measurements
brief: Read N integers, write them to readings.txt, close it, reopen for reading, and report the first and last saved values.
hints: Open with mode w, check fopen, and save one number per line.
Close and reopen in mode r.
Read back to EOF, remembering first and last.

title: Append measurements safely
brief: Keep the first batch in readings.txt. Append M more values with mode a, reopen and count all saved records as well as first and last.
input: N (1–10), N integers [-100,100], M (0–10), then M integers [-100,100].
hints: Write and close the initial file first.
Use a new fopen with append mode to preserve existing lines.
Count all values during the final read.

title: Recursive sum to N
brief: Implement int sumTo(int n) recursively for 1+...+n, with sumTo(0)=0. Use no loops in the function.
hints: Define the n=0 base case.
Reduce n by one in each call.
Return n + sumTo(n-1).

title: Recursive sum of squares
brief: Keep sumTo(n) and add recursive squaresTo(n)=1²+...+n². Show both results.
hints: Use n=0 as the new base case.
The recurrence adds n*n to squaresTo(n-1).
Keep the two recursive functions separate.

title: A tiny command stack
brief: Simulate a stack of up to 10 integers. '+' followed by an integer pushes, '-' pops. The input guarantees no overflow or underflow.
input: K (0–20) commands, each '+' then integer [-100,100], or '-'. Commands stay inside capacity 10.
output: size=N top=V, with top=-1 for an empty stack.
hints: Use a fixed int array and a size counter.
Push at array[size] then increase size.
Pop by decreasing size; top is array[size-1] if size > 0.

title: Stack safety under bad commands
brief: Process arbitrary push/pop commands while preserving capacity 10. Ignore a push on full or pop on empty; count all rejected operations.
input: K (0–40) commands, each '+' then integer [-100,100], or '-'.
output: size=N top=V rejected=R, with top=-1 if empty.
hints: Check full and empty conditions before mutating size.
Still read the number of a rejected push.
Keep a counter for every rejected operation.
